This mod is a sub-mod for Ethics and Civics: Bug Branch that adds 40 new branch-office buildings. These buildings are primarily second and third tiers for existing buildings, which give more jobs for the branch-office host, and more resources for the branch-office owner. The resources given scale based on the number of appropriate jobs on the host planet e.g. metallurgists for Private Shipyards.

Criminal branch-office buildings have been entirely reworked, with the jobs they give now belonging to the criminal strata, with the branch-office host only receiving any resources if the planet has the Deal with Crime Lords decision active.

An updated version of the original mod, uploaded with Toaster's Permission. As with the original mod, this mod aims to make raiding bombardment worth the effort.

Mod Features:
	- Every pop you abduct gives 25 trade, minerals, energy, food, alloys, and consumer goods
	- Despoilation and Pirate Raid war goal also gives trade, consumer goods and alloys, and gives 500 resources on status quo
	- Despoilation and Pirate Raid war goal also gives motes/gases/crystals, assuming the target as the techs for them
	- Despoilation and Pirate Raid wars gives half as much war exhaustion
	- Letters of Marque gives +50% Material Liberator and Shipbreaker rewards
	-  Voidreaver gains access to the Pirate Raid CB

Overview
I wanted to tweak several planetary modifiers to provide more flavorful and useful bonuses.

[*]The C.A.R.E Interactive Interface is an economic optimization engine, so I wanted it to give a bonus to trade value
[*]The Extensive Moon System modifier adds mining districts and output... to gas giants which can't be colonized, so I changed it to give a bonus to mining stations (but not research stations) that also applies to any unhabitable moons, and moved the bonus mineral jobs production and mining districts onto any/all habitable moons
[*]The Resource Consolidation origin goes through all the trouble of shrinking gas giants and converting them to molten worlds tagged with the "Chthonian Planet" modifier but then a game start event clears all modifiers, so I wanted to stop blanket deleting planetary modifiers in starting systems
[*]Allow multiple planetary modifiers to spawn on any given planet, as suggested by the majority of the planetary modifier spawn code (which weights some higher or lower in the presence of other planetary modifiers)
[*]Convert all the "mineral richness" related modifiers to provide bonuses to the miner job category (rather than only minerals production) and mining station output, similar to the changes for #2

Compatibility
This mod should be fairly compatible with other mods. Incompatibilities would likely occur if other mods also overwrite or add same the planetary or static modifier IDs. If another mod is attempting to specify the same modifiers: first in wins for static modifiers, but last in wins for planetary modifiers. This mod overwrites 8 different static modifiers and 23 planetary modifiers.

This mod also overrides a game setup event game_setup.2. I find it unlikely other mods would be changing this event (it clears planetary modifiers for home systems); in any case first in wins for events.

Built for Stellaris version 3.8 "Gemini." Not compatible with achievements. Largely compatible with Guilli's Planet Modifiers and Features - Guilli's static modifier changes will take precedence but there are no error-causing conflicts. Also has built-in compatibility with Planetary Diversity.

When to Install
This mod can be safely added to your save after the game has started, but not removed. If this mod is not active at game start, you will miss out of the Extensive Moon System (Moon) modifier being applied to the moons of gas giants with Extensive Moon System and minerals being added to some planets with modifiers but no deposits. Removing this mod will result in unknown planetary modifiers - which Stellaris may or may not handle gracefully.

WH40k Planets Renewed

Compatibility
Game Version:  3.14.15
Not compatible with 4.0 yet (working on it)

Permission
This mod was created using the New Planets WH40k mod created by kamip123 and is being posted with the permission of the original creator.  The original mod was updated by kanip123 to 2.8.1 and can be found [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=850823920]here.

What the Mod Does

In brief, this mod updates the original 40k planets mod by doing several things.

1. Changes the method of creating the 40k planets from terraforming to a planetary decision like the ecumenopolis in the vanilla game.
2. Changes the requirements for building these planets in order to somewhat gatekeep till mid-game as once these planets become functional the economy derived from them can rival an aggressive mega/giga structure building program.
3. Adds new unique districts for all the worlds so create a more immersive and rewarding feel.
4. Added and changed bonuses on many of the worlds.  I was going to draw up a spreadsheet on the changes but they are numerous and I don't have the time right now.
5. Made some modifications to the way you progress through the planets.  There are planets that are stand-alone, meaning they aren't meant to have be upgraded to a forge/hiveworld such as an Agri World or Fortress World.  Then there are planets that chain a series of upgrades together to progress in stages to a final state. The big two are as follows:

The Industrial World upgrades to either a Forge World, Refinery World, or an Armory World.  Each of these worlds then upgrades to their type of world with an Iron Ring.

The Small Hive World upgrades to either a Medium Hive World, or an Industrial Hive World and these worlds then upgrade to a Super Hive World and a Mega Hive World.

IMPORTANT NOTE!  The district upkeep for the upgraded worlds become very costly.  This cost is offset by the Refinery World production and should be one of the first worlds you upgrade to.

Personally, I always found Stellaris's armies to be a bit bland, lacking variety. The aim of this mod is to add this missing variety. I'm *very* new to Stellaris modding and modding in general, so if you find any bugs, please let me know.

This mod is a work in progress and currently has 22 armies. If you have any ideas for armies or any requests, comment them down below.

@ means Hive Only
R means Robotic
M means mechanical empires only

The 22 currently added are:
Special Forces: "Deploy the hyper-lethal." -Anonymous Officer
 An improved version of the normal assault armies. Has higher morale and damage, but lower health due to the special forces having less members than a normal army. Does not require research, and is fairly costly.

Armored Division: "We're breaking in, boys!" -Anonymous Gunner
A much more powerful version of the normal army, having higher stats across the board except for morale. Incredibly expensive and hard to maintain. Inflicts high morale damage due to the imposing nature of armored vehicles. Does not require research, and is very costly.

Scorcher Division: "I just wanna grill in peace!" -Anonymous Scorcher
A terror unit, designed to damage enemy morale. Deals slightly more damage than a normal army, but it really shines in its morale damage, its collateral damage, and its cost. Requires first level of plasma throwers to unlock.

Super Soldiers: "Yes general, I *am* the reinforcements." - 
An improved version of the Gene Seed Warriors, being much more powerful in every stat. Inflicts higher morale damage due to the reputation of the super soldiers. Requires gene seed purification and is ludicrously expensive.

Space Marines: "Get off my ship, space marines!"
An improved assault army, having higher health and damage, but has much higher morale. Where it really shines is in its 10 times extra collateral damage, to really help you purge those xenos. High cost, high upkeep, and requires the Combat Training tech to unlock.

Mech Troopers: "Yeehaw!" - Anonymous Mech Trooper
An improved armored division, having higher stats across the board. Consists of large exo suits (think Titans from Titanfall) piloted by elite armored division personnel. High cost, high upkeep, and requires the Exo Suit technology to unlock.

Fighter Bombers: "Napalm, high explosives, bunker busters. Take your pick." - Anonymous Pilot
Supersonic atmospheric fighter bombers, having higher damage and morale damage due to the terrifying nature of air bombing campaigns. Has 5 times extra collateral damage to really tear up a planet. Has high health to represent the difficult nature of shooting down supersonic jets. Requires carrier operations.

Grunts: "Fix bayonets!" - Anonymous Commisar
A division of almost entirely basic infantry. Unlike the normal assault army, this doesn't include the support necessary for infantry, making them inexpensive but weaker. Very cheap, quick to train, and require no research.

(R) Automated Armor: "*Unintelligible mechanized gurgling*" - Robot dude
A division of autonomous tanks, being weaker than the standard tanks but not suffering from morale penalties and is slightly cheaper. Requires at least one robot pop on the planet.

Grenadiers: "Now that they got grenades, they think they're better than us!" - Anonymous Grunt
A division of better equipped and better trained soldiers. This makes them more expensive but slightly more powerful than the standard assault army. Deals slightly more collateral damage due to the nature of explosives. Requires combat training.

(@) Ravenous Swarm: "Those who do not share our vision do not get to see its glory." - Hive Leader
Horrible mutated creatures from the depths of the hive labs. Incredibly weak and easy to kill, but breed incredibly fast. Armies of millions can swarm and overwhelm the most powerful of soldiers. *Very* cheap and train in 14 days, but weakest unit in the game.

(@) Vile Cannon: "Watch yourself, the dust out here may be hostile." - Anonymous Sergeant
Brutal cannons that shoot swarms of small insect-like creatures that swarm and then tear apart soldiers. When in large enough groups, they can take down jets or even tanks. The cannons themselves are relatively defenseless and upon a cannon's death, all of its swarm dies.
